project: Self-Evolving Explainable Rational Agent for Adaptive Industrial Decision Intelligence Using Statistical Trend Learning
evaluation_unit_cautions: All-cycle and final-cycle metrics are not directly interchangeable.
Validation and test results must be reported separately.
Small engine-level validation samples give uncertain safety estimates.
Illustrative maintenance costs are not industrial cost evidence.
Distribution shift is not, by itself, proof of temporal concept drift.
A completed audit does not establish model correctness or deployment safety.

CSV has headers or content but contains zero data rows.
All-cycle validation metrics and final-cycle engine metrics are different evaluation units. Do not compare them as though they measured the same set of observations.
Calibration is post-processing fitted using training-partition out-of-fold predictions. It is not model retraining. Review the saved report and metrics before making improvement claims.
Maintenance costs are illustrative assumptions, not validated industrial cost estimates.
The final-cycle validation policy evidence involves only 20 engines. Zero observed misses does not establish zero real-world failure risk.
Training-to-test sensor distribution differences do not alone prove temporal concept drift, causal degradation, or policy failure.

Policy selection, calibration, drift detection, and auditing do not by themselves demonstrate continuous online learning. A controlled feedback-loop experiment is still needed to support a strong self-evolution claim.
Test-set metrics are for final reporting only. Do not use them to tune models, calibration, thresholds, or claims.
